title: Guardian canonical event v1
description: One thing that happened at a decoy, in the shape every later stage reads. EV-02 fixes the field set; this is that list made checkable. The envelope carries metadata and a reference to raw evidence, never the raw evidence itself: EV-03 bounds what is retained and where, and an envelope that could hold a transcript would put an attacker's bytes in every index that touches it.

schema.description: The contract version. A mismatch is explicit and fatal at ingest; an event written to another contract is never partially read.

event_id.description: AC-EV-001. Stable across retries and replay: the Edge assigns it once, at capture, and a redelivery carries the same value so ingest can refuse the duplicate. It is never regenerated on send, because an identifier minted per attempt makes at-least-once delivery indistinguishable from repeated attacks.

event_time.description: AC-EV-003. When the interaction happened, as the decoy's clock saw it.

observed_time.description: AC-EV-003. When the Edge's adapter saw it. Distinct from event_time because a log adapter reads a file some time after the line was written, and collapsing the two would hide that delay.

ingested_time.description: AC-EV-003. When the Control Plane accepted it. Set by the Control Plane and by nothing else: an Edge that could assert its own ingest time could backdate an event past a retention boundary. Absent on the wire from the Edge, present once stored.

edge_id.description: Which Edge reported. Taken from the authenticated device identity at ingest and never from a field the Edge fills, so one Edge cannot attribute an event to another.

source_ip.description: Who connected. Observed from the connection, not parsed from attacker-supplied text where the path allows it; a log adapter that reads it from a line must treat it as untrusted and this field's bounds are what keeps a malformed line from becoming an unbounded string.

destination_ip.description: The decoy's own address, which is Guardian's and therefore trustworthy.

protocol.description: The closed DC-01 family set, plus the transport for events that are not application-level.

action.description: What the interaction was. A closed vocabulary rather than free text, because a console renders it as a category and an adapter that could invent one would be putting attacker-influenced strings into a category field.

session_id.description: Groups events from one attacker session. Adapter-assigned and bounded; it is not a Guardian identity and nothing may resolve it to one.

auth.description: Who the attacker claimed to be and whether the decoy accepted it. There is deliberately no field for the secret they supplied: EV-03 requires credential material to be protected or redacted, and an envelope with nowhere to put a password cannot leak one into an index, a log line, or a console.

identity.description: The username or account the attacker offered. Attacker-controlled, bounded, and untrusted to any renderer.

synthetic_credential_id.description: Set when the offered credential matched one Guardian planted (P2-W9). It names the planted credential, never the secret, so a match is provable without storing what was typed.

raw_ref.description: Where the bounded raw evidence lives, if any was kept. A reference and never the bytes: EV-03 keeps HTTP bodies and SSH transcripts bounded and stored separately, and P2-W13 owns the blob and quarantine paths. An event with no retained evidence has no reference, which is different from having an empty one.

truncated.description: Whether EV-03's bound cut the evidence short. Recorded rather than inferred, so a reader never mistakes a truncated transcript for a complete one.

quarantined.description: Whether the raw material was quarantined instead of stored for normal retrieval. EV-03 quarantines binary uploads where supported.

sensitivity.description: What the referenced evidence holds, which is what access and retention are decided from. Ordered: routine carries metadata only; sensitive carries bounded captured content; restricted means credential material was involved, and the event records the identity and result while the secret itself was never stored.

provenance.description: AC-EV-002: from an evidence item, the edge, decoy, runtime, schema, and raw reference must be visible. The first two and the schema are top-level fields; this carries the rest, plus which of P2-W11's two paths produced the event — a native typed path and a third-party log parser do not warrant the same confidence, and a reader is entitled to know which one this came through.
